articles.title: Pope Leo XIV on White Sox return to postseason: 'Great things happen in Chicago'
articles.summary: The White Sox have not won a playoff since series claiming the 2005 World Series title.
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox are back in the playoffs after clinching a spot on Thursday with a 9-1 win over the Kansas City Royals . The postseason appearance ends a five-year drought for the franchise, which had three-straight 100-loss seasons entering the 2026 campaign.

There were a number of factors that went into the successful regular season such as the offensive production from Miguel Vargas , Colson Montgomery and offseason addition Munetaka Murakami , as well as the pitching staff led by Sean Burke .

Another potential factor is the power of long-time White Sox fan Robert Prevost, better known now as Pope Leo XIV.

The Holy Father's fandom has been heavily documented, as he was in attendance at the 2005 World Series , which the White Sox won.

So would Pope Leo's new status have anything to do with the turnaround season for his favorite baseball team?

"No comment," Leo said , smiling when asked on the papal plane. "Great things happen in Chicago ."

The team and the fanbase have embraced their famous fan since he became Pope. As the playoffs get set to begin next week, everyone on the South Side of Chicago is hoping Leo's good luck will lead to a championship parade at the end of October.

articles.title: Red Sox vs. Yankees Set for 2026 MLB Playoffs Bracket, Updated Standings Ahead of Postseason
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox and New York Yankees will renew their rivalry in the Wild Card round of the 2026 MLB playoffs.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox and New York Yankees will renew their rivalry in the Wild Card round of the 2026 MLB playoffs.

The Red Sox locked in the matchup Thursday with a 4-3 win over the visiting Chicago Cubs.

The Red Sox are now set to travel to the Bronx for Game 1 of the Wild Card series next Tuesday.

The teams will return Wednesday for Game 2 and, if necessary, could finish out the series Thursday with a winner-takes-all Game 3. All three games will be broadcast on NBC/NBCSN and stream on Peacock.

This marks the seventh time the Red Sox and Yankees have met one another in the postseason, with the most recent matchup taking place during the 2025 Wild Card series.

The Yankees lost the opening game of that series before coming back to win Game 2.

Then-Yankees pitcher Garrett Crochet helped his club close out the Game 3 win and become the third team in history to advance to the divisional series after opening the postseason with a Wild Card loss.

The Yankees went 7-6 against the Red Sox (4-2 at home) this season, securing the regular-season series victory with a 16-1 blowout Aug. 30 at Yankee Stadium.

The home team is heading into the matchup with an intimidating pitching rotation led by Gerrit Cole, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón but potentially missing Aaron Judge, who could miss the Wild Card round with a right calf strain.

The Red Sox have some injury questions of their own with closer Aroldis Chapman and outfielder Ceddanne Rafaela both dealing with recent health issues, but Boston also boasts a strong top-of-the rotation in Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray and Ranger Suarez.

These clubs, which have put together two of the most efficient rotations in MLB this season, could be set for a pitching duel when Game 1 starts this Tuesday at a time yet to be determined.

articles.title: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Apologizes for Remarks on $500M Blue Jays Contract, 'I Regret My Comments'
articles.summary: Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. sparked backlash after recent comments regarding the 14-year, $500 million contract extension he signed last offseason, and now the six-time All-Star is profusely apologizing for his remarks as his tough 2026 campaign nears its end.
articles.body:
Toronto Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. sparked backlash after recent comments regarding the 14-year, $500 million contract extension he signed last offseason, and now the six-time All-Star is profusely apologizing for his remarks as his tough 2026 campaign nears its end.

B/R's Undisputed MLB Outfielder Rankings 🔢

Pope Leo jokes about White Sox playoff return

During an interview with Veronica Batista on the program, "Grandes Ligas," Guerrero had this to say (Spanish-to-English translation via ESPN ):

"I want people to understand one thing. The money they gave me wasn't for what I'm going to do. It was for what I already did," Guerrero told Batista. "They didn't pay me because I'm going to hit 40 [home runs] every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished. People are confused about that, but I think the same way they do. Like, sometimes I even say to myself, 'Bro, they gave you all that money and you're out here doing nothing.' But I try.

"You know how it is with fans, when you're good, they're with you 100%. But when you smell like s---, like we like to say here, nobody supports you. The ones who support you are the ones who stay with you. Those are my real fans and I considered them my family."

Last year, Guerrero nearly helped guide the Blue Jays to their first World Series title since 1993. He hit .292 (.848 OPS) with 23 home runs and 84 RBI before following that up with a scorching-hot postseason (eight home runs, 17 RBI, .397 average, 1.289 OPS).

However, this season has been a nightmare for Guerrero and the last-place Jays. The eight-year veteran's numbers have dipped significantly (nine home runs, 56 RBI, .263 average, .695 OPS).

As John Henry of MLB.com noted, Guerrero has dealt with back and hamstring issues during this season. He also suffered a concussion after a collision with New York Yankees shortstop George Lombard Jr.

Naturally, Blue Jays fans may not want to hear that Guerrero was paid for his past accomplishments, considering (a) his performance and (b) the length and money on his upcoming contract years.

Guerrero initially doubled down on his initial remarks.

"No, I don't regret myself. I'm not lying with what I say," Guerrero said via an interpreter, per ESPN. "I understand some fans, they don't understand the way and what I was trying to say specifically, but what I said is the way I feel."

However, Guerrero has since changed his stance.

The 2026 season was a lost one for a Blue Jays squad that saw a host of players regress after a tremendous and magical 2025 campaign.

Next season, should there be one in the face of a potential lockout, brings new hope that this team, led by Guerrero, can meet its ceiling and bounce back.

articles.title: Blue Jays' Vladimir Guerrero Jr. apologizes for comments about $500 million contract and fan support amid subpar season
articles.summary: Guerrero heard from his Hall of Fame father, who told him that his remarks were wrong and he needed to apologize for them.
articles.body:
Vladimir Guerrero Jr . didn't have a good 2026 season for the Toronto Blue Jays .

But to prevent the disappointing season from ending on a bitter note, one which could have lingered into the offseason, the six-time All-Star is apologizing for comments he made to a Spanish-language reporter. In the interview, Guerrero was defensive about the 14-year, $500 million contract extension he signed last year and whether he's fulfilling the expectations that blockbuster deal established.

"The money they gave me wasn't for what I'm going to do. It was for what I already did," Guerrero said in an interview with Veronica Batista of Noticias Telemicro ( via MLB.com ). "They didn't pay me because I'm going to hit 40 every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished."

Guerrero went on to say "real fans" were the ones that supported him even when he has a subpar performance.

"The fans, I know how they are," he added ( translated by reporter Héctor Gómez ). "When you are doing great, they are 100% behind you, but when you are not at your best, not everybody is behind you, almost nobody supports you. Those are my real fans, the ones that are supporting me all the time."

The Blue Jays first baseman followed up by saying he didn't regret those statements . As could be expected, fans didn't receive those remarks well. That led to him apologizing on Friday.

"I regret my comments the other day," Guerrero Jr. told reporters through an interpreter, via SportsNet . "I felt from my heart that my fans and my teammates needed an apology from me. I'm going to continue working hard to make my contract great."

Either Guerrero realized that what he said was poorly received or someone enlightened him. It appears to have been the latter. The eight-year veteran said that his father, Hall of Famer Vladimir Guerrero, told him that he made a mistake.

"He told me what I did was wrong and to make sure that I do what I'm doing right now — to give my fans an apology," he said, via SportsNet.

Guerrero has only nine home runs going into this weekend's final three-game series with the Cincinnati Reds . But even if he reaches double digits to go with his .263/.335/.360 slash line, that is far below the production expected from a former 40-homer slugger who's being paid an average of $35 million per year.

The Blue Jays followed up last year's World Series appearance with a losing record. Depending on how Toronto plays in its final three games, they will finish in either fourth or fifth place in the American League East. If Guerrero hit up to his standards, perhaps the season would have had a different outcome.

Yet a fresh start next season would have been more difficult if fans held resentment to the Blue Jays' top player. Obviously, hitting 25 to 30 home runs would turn perception around. But apologizing could also help win at least some of those supporters back.

articles.title: Red Sox move final game of series vs. Cubs to Tampa Bay's Tropicana Field to avoid nor'easter
articles.summary: The threat of inclement weather had already forced Boston and Chicago to play a doubleheader on Friday.
articles.body:
A massive nor'easter has led the Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs to take drastic measures for their regular-season finale. The league is moving the final game of the series from Fenway Park to the Tampa Bay Rays ' Tropicana Field in order to avoid the storm, which is set to hit the northeastern United States this weekend.

The game, which was originally scheduled for 7:15 p.m. ET Saturday, will instead take place at 3:05 p.m. Sunday in Tampa . The Red Sox announced the move on Friday, shortly before the second game of a doubleheader between the Sox and Cubs. Tickets will be fully refunded, per the team.

Friday's Cubs-Sox doubleheader was also a choice made because of the storm. Earlier this week, the league adjusted the series by moving Sunday's game to Friday as part of a doubleheader . Both teams will travel to Florida after the conclusion of the second game Friday, "to ensure the safety of both traveling parties," per the Sox.

In a statement, Rays CEO Ken Babby said the team is "proud to support" MLB by hosting the game, citing a desire to help "ensure fans can enjoy this matchup despite the weather challenges in the Northeast," via Ryan Bass of MLB.TV .

Babby noted that the Rays are familiar with weather challenges, as the team had to play the entire 2025 season in an alternate venue after Tropicana Field's roof was heavily damaged by Hurricane Milton in 2024.

"When Tropicana Field was damaged, clubs throughout the league stepped up to support our organization during an incredibly challenging time," Babby said, via Bass. "We're grateful for that solidarity and are pleased to return the favor by welcoming the Cubs, Red Sox, and their fans to Tropicana Field on Sunday."

This weekend's nor'easter is set to bring high winds and heavy rain across the northeast, with potential floods expected along the coasts. Multiple advisories have been issued by the National Weather Service , starting Friday and running through Sunday.

Boston is not the only area that is expected to be affected: The storm will hit New York as well, which led the Yankees to adjust their final regular-season series , too. The Yankees, hosting the Baltimore Orioles this weekend, switched to a doubleheader on Friday, with the final game of the series still set to take place in the Bronx on Sunday.
